lines: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009. For the most part, the response has been **favorable**. "Hooray! At last!" wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic.

lines: One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known. Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert's appointment in the Times, calls him "an unpretentious musician with no air of the **formidable** conductor about him." As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as **faint praise**.
然而，这一任命之所以令人意外，原因之一是吉尔伯特相对而言鲜为人知。甚至曾在《纽约时报》上撰文支持任命吉尔伯特的托马西尼也称他为“一位不事张扬的音乐家，身上没有威严指挥家的气场”。对于一个迄今为止曾由古斯塔夫·马勒和皮埃尔·布列兹等音乐家执掌的乐团的下任音乐总监来说，这样的描述在至少一些《纽约时报》读者看来恐怕算不上什么**高度的赞美**。

lines: For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one. To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting **orchestral** music. All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from **iTunes**.

lines: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point. For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century. These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today's live performances; moreover, they can be "**consumed**" at a time and place of the listener's choosing. The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert.

那些忠实的音乐会常客反驳说，录音制品无法替代现场演出，但他们没有抓住问题的实质。为了赢得艺术爱好者的时间、关注和金钱，古典器乐演奏家不仅要与歌剧院、舞蹈团、剧团和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪伟大古典音乐家的录音演出竞争。这些唱片价格便宜，随处可得，而且其艺术水准常常远高于如今的现场演出；此外，听众还可以在自己选择的时间和地点“**欣赏**”它们。因此，这类唱片的广泛流传已经给传统古典音乐会体制带来了一场危机。

lines: One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record. Gilbert's own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into "a markedly different, more **vibrant** organization." But what will be the nature of that difference? Merely expanding the orchestral **repertoire** will not be enough. If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America's oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.

lines: When Liam McGee departed as president of Bank of America in August, his explanation was surprisingly straight up. Rather than cloaking his exit in the usual vague excuses, he came right out and said he was leaving "to pursue my goal of running a company." Broadcasting his ambition was "very much my **decision**," McGee says. Within two weeks, he was talking for the first time with the board of Hartford Financial Services Group, which named him CEO and chairman on September 29.
当利亚姆·麦基八月份从美国银行总裁任上离职时，他的解释出奇地直截了当。他没有用通常那种含糊其辞的借口来掩饰自己的离开，而是直言不讳地说，他离开是为了“追求我执掌一家公司的目标”。麦基说，公开宣扬自己的抱负“完全是我自己的**决定**”。不到两周，他就与哈特福德金融服务集团的董事会进行了首次会谈，该集团于9月29日任命他为首席执行官兼董事长。

lines: McGee says leaving without a position lined up gave him time to reflect on what kind of company he wanted to run. It also sent a clear message to the outside world about his **aspirations**. And McGee isn't alone. In recent weeks the No.2 executives at Avon and American Express quit with the explanation that they were looking for a CEO post. As boards scrutinize succession plans in response to shareholder pressure, executives who don't get the nod also may wish to move on. A turbulent business environment also has senior managers cautious of letting vague pronouncements cloud their **reputations**.

lines: The rough guide to marketing success used to be that you got what you paid for. No longer. While traditional "**paid**" media — such as television commercials and print advertisements — still play a major role, companies today can exploit many alternative forms of media. Consumers passionate about a product may create "**earned**" media by willingly promoting it to friends, and a company may leverage "owned" media by sending e-mail alerts about products and sales to customers registered with its Web site. The way consumers now approach the process of making purchase decisions means that marketing's impact stems from a broad range of factors beyond conventional **paid** media.

营销成功的粗略法则过去是“一分钱一分货”。如今不再如此。虽然传统“**付费**”媒体——如电视广告和平面广告——仍然扮演重要角色，但当今企业可以利用许多其他形式的媒体。热衷于某种产品的消费者可能通过自愿向朋友推荐来创造“**口碑**”媒体；企业则可以利用“自有”媒体，向在其网站注册的用户发送产品和促销信息的电子邮件提醒。如今消费者作出购买决策的方式意味着，营销的影响力来自传统付费媒体之外的众多因素。

lines: Paid and owned media are controlled by marketers promoting their own products. For earned media, such marketers act as the initiator for users' responses. But in some cases, one marketer's owned media become another marketer's paid media—for instance, when an e-commerce retailer sells ad space on its Web site. We define such **sold** media as owned media whose traffic is so strong that other organizations place their content or e-commerce engines within that environment. This trend, which we believe is still in its infancy, effectively began with retailers and travel providers such as airlines and hotels and will no doubt go further. Johnson & Johnson, for example, has created BabyCenter, a stand-alone media property that promotes complementary and even competitive products. Besides generating income, the presence of other marketers makes the site seem objective, gives companies opportunities to learn valuable information about the appeal of other companies' marketing, and may help expand user **traffic** for all companies concerned.

付费媒体和自有媒体由推销自己产品的营销者控制。而对于口碑媒体，这些营销者只是用户反应的发起者。但在某些情况下，一家营销者的自有媒体会成为另一家营销者的付费媒体——例如，电子商务零售商出售其网站上的广告位时。我们将这种**售出**媒体定义为：流量大到足以让其他机构在其环境中放置内容或电子商务引擎的自有媒体。我们认为这一趋势尚处于初期阶段，它实际上始于零售商以及航空、酒店等旅行服务商，并且无疑会走得更远。例如，强生公司创建了BabyCenter，一个推广互补产品乃至竞争产品的独立媒体资产。除带来收入外，其他营销者的存在使该网站显得客观，为企业提供了了解其他公司营销吸引力的宝贵信息，并可能帮助所有相关公司扩大用户**流量**。

lines: The same dramatic technological changes that have provided marketers with more (and more diverse) communications choices have also increased the risk that passionate consumers will voice their opinions in quicker, more visible, and much more damaging ways. Such **hijacked** media are the opposite of earned media: an asset or campaign becomes hostage to consumers, other stakeholders, or activists who make negative allegations about a brand or product. Members of social networks, for instance, are learning that they can hijack media to apply pressure on the businesses that originally created them.
为营销者提供了更多（且更多样）传播选择的巨大技术变革，同时也加大了这样的风险：热情的消费者会以更快、更显眼、破坏性大得多的方式表达自己的意见。这种被**劫持**的媒体与口碑媒体正好相反：某项资产或营销活动被消费者、其他利益相关者或活动人士劫为人质，他们对该品牌或产品作出负面指控。例如，社交网络的成员们逐渐意识到，他们可以劫持媒体，向最初创建这些媒体的企业施压。

lines: It's no surprise that Jennifer Senior's insightful, provocative magazine cover story, "I love My Children, I Hate My Life," is arousing much chatter — nothing gets people talking like the suggestion that child rearing is anything less than a completely **fulfilling**, life-enriching experience. Rather than concluding that children make parents either happy or miserable, Senior suggests we need to redefine happiness: instead of thinking of it as something that can be measured by moment-to-moment joy, we should consider being happy as a past-tense condition. Even though the day-to-day experience of raising kids can be soul-**crushingly** hard, Senior writes that "the very things that in the moment dampen our moods can later be sources of intense gratification and delight."

珍妮弗·西尼尔见解深刻、颇具争议性的杂志封面文章《我爱我的孩子，我恨我的生活》引发热烈讨论，这毫不奇怪——没有什么比暗示养育孩子并非完全**令人满足**、丰富人生的体验更能激起人们的议论了。西尼尔并没有下结论说孩子使父母幸福或痛苦，而是提出我们需要重新定义幸福：幸福不应被看作可以用时时刻刻的快乐来衡量的东西，而应被视为一种过去时态的状态。尽管抚养孩子的日常体验可能艰难到令人心碎，西尼尔写道：“正是那些当下令我们情绪低落的事情，日后会成为强烈满足感和欢乐的源泉。”

lines: In a society that so persistently celebrates **procreation**, is it any wonder that admitting you regret having children is equivalent to admitting you support kitten-killing? It doesn't seem quite fair, then, to compare the regrets of parents to the regrets of the childless. Unhappy parents rarely are provoked to wonder if they shouldn't have had kids, but unhappy childless folks are bothered with the message that children are the single most important thing in the world: obviously their misery must be a direct result of the gaping baby-size holes in their lives.

lines: With its theme that "Mind is the master **weaver**, creating our inner character and outer circumstances," the book As a Man Thinketh by James Allen is an in-depth exploration of the central idea of self-help writing. (46) Allen's contribution was to take an assumption we all share — that because we are not robots we therefore control our thoughts — and reveal its erroneous nature. Because most of us believe that mind is separate from matter, we think that thoughts can be hidden and made powerless; this allows us to think one way and act another. However, Allen believed that the unconscious mind generates as much action as the conscious mind, and (47) while we may be able to sustain the **illusion** of control through the conscious mind alone, in reality we are continually faced with a question: "Why cannot I make myself do this or achieve that?"

《人的思考》一书以“心灵是编织大师，编织出我们内在的性格与外在的环境”为主题，对自助类写作的核心思想进行了深入探讨。(46) 艾伦的贡献在于，他选取了我们共有的一个假设——因为我们不是机器人，所以能控制自己的思想——并揭示了其错误的本质。因为我们大多数人相信精神与物质是分离的，所以认为思想可以被隐藏起来并使之失去效力；这就使我们得以这样想、那样做。然而，艾伦认为，潜意识与意识一样能够支配我们的行为，而且(47) 尽管我们或许可以仅凭意识来维持“掌控自我”的幻觉，但现实中我们却不断面临一个问题：“我为什么不能让自己做这件事或实现那个目标？”

data.title: 图画作文：旅程之"余"
data.directions_en: 52. Directions: Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. (20 points)
data.directions_zh: 52. 题目要求：根据下图写一篇160—200词的文章。文章中，你应当：1）简要描述图画；2）解释其寓意；3）发表你的评论。请工整地写在答题卡2上。（20分）
data.image_desc: 图画标题为"旅程之'余'"：两名游客坐在船上游览湖光山色，却一边吃一边随手把果皮、饭盒、饮料瓶等垃圾扔进湖中，湖面已漂浮着不少杂物，与周围的青山绿水形成鲜明反差。
sample: The drawing presents a scene that is as ironic as it is familiar. Two tourists are sitting in a boat enjoying the beautiful scenery of a lake. Yet, while feasting themselves on food, they are casually tossing the leftovers — plastic boxes, bottles and wrappers — into the water, which is already dotted with floating rubbish. Beneath the picture is a thought-provoking caption: "The 'leftovers' of the journey."
这幅图画展现了一个既熟悉又颇具讽刺意味的场景。两名游客正坐在船上游览美丽的湖光山色。然而，他们一边大快朵颐，一边随手把剩饭剩菜——塑料盒、瓶子和包装纸——扔进湖里，湖面上已经漂满了垃圾。图下是一句发人深省的标题：“旅程之“余””。

sample: The intended meaning of the cartoon is not difficult to perceive: it exposes the **uncivilized** behavior of some tourists who take pleasure from nature but repay it with pollution. In their eyes, the beauty of the scenic spots is a free resource to be enjoyed, not a treasure to be protected. Such conduct, however, damages the environment that future generations will inherit, and it tarnishes the image of tourism itself. What the picture calls "leftovers" is, in essence, the residue of **selfishness** and the lack of public morality.
这幅漫画的寓意不难领会：它揭露了一些游客的不**文明**行为——他们从大自然中获得愉悦，却以污染来回报自然。在他们眼里，风景名胜只是一种可供享用的免费资源，而不是需要保护的珍宝。然而，这种行为破坏了子孙后代将要继承的环境，也玷污了旅游业自身的形象。图中所说的“余”，实质上是**自私**与公德缺失的残渣。

sample: In my view, enjoying the beauty of nature and preserving it should go hand in hand. On the one hand, the government and tourist sites should enforce rules and impose penalties on those who litter, and provide more convenient facilities for waste disposal.
